input:
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen react over a copper-zinc oxide catalyst to give formaldehyde, and the form in which the catalyst is used sets both the yield obtained from a given catalyst volume and the pressure drop across the bed. Structured and pellet forms of the catalyst are compared at one feed composition, at 230 °C and 60 bar, with a feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3. The structured catalyst gives the higher yield at the lower pressure drop, and it loses activity more slowly over the test.

Space-time yield is the mass of product per unit catalyst volume per hour. The structured catalyst gives a space-time yield of 1 kg L-1 h-1, against 0.31 kg L-1 h-1 for the pellet catalyst. Pressure drop is 0.18 bar for the structured catalyst and 1.51 bar for the pellet catalyst, and activity loss after 100 h is 6% for the structured catalyst and 17% for the pellet catalyst. On the three measures reported, the structured form is ahead on each one.

The comparison covers the single feed composition tested, and no sulfur-bearing feed was tested. Yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge, so the values reported here cannot be set against a matched pair of values from other reports on this catalyst.
